subject: Architecture
title: The Millennium Bridge: London's Wobble
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Millennium Bridge: London's Wobble.

hook.text: London's Millennium Bridge opened in June 2000 — and closed two days later because it swayed dangerously.

buildup.text: The sleek, low-profile suspension footbridge was designed by Norman Foster and sculptor Anthony Caro.

discovery.text: When pedestrians walked, their footsteps synchronized with the bridge's sway — amplifying the wobble.

twist.text: This 'synchronous lateral excitation' had never been studied — it wasn't in any engineering textbook.

climax.text: Engineers installed 91 dampers to absorb the motion. The bridge reopened in 2002 and hasn't wobbled since.

punchline.text: People walk in sync. Nobody knew that could break a bridge.

quiz.question: What caused the Millennium Bridge to wobble?
options: Wind forces on the bridge's flat profile
Pedestrians' footsteps synchronized with the bridge's sway
Tidal forces from the River Thames pushed the foundations
